rationale: Both texts narrate the same baptism, checkable directly by reading the two side by side. Luke's wording of the divine voice matches Mark's second-person form exactly ("You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased", BSB), and so stands in the same relationship to Matthew's own third-person wording ("This is My beloved Son") already reported in the connection to Mark 1:9-11. Luke alone adds two details absent from both Matthew and Mark: Jesus "was praying" as heaven opened (3:21), and the Spirit descended "in a bodily form like a dove" (3:22) -- a specific claim about the form of the sign that neither Matthew's nor Mark's wording states. Matthew's own account of John's objection and Jesus's answer (3:14-15) has no counterpart in Luke's account either. The label is strong rather than explicit because neither Gospel names or cites the other as its source for this scene.
